title: His father made him play cornet in an adult band
summary: Howard says his father insisted he play cornet with adults when he was ten to twelve, and forced it with slaps.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: (Unintelligible)
(Unintelligible)
Can we go back?
Sure.
About you saying your father wanted you to play and you didn't really want to stick with the cornet but can you explain what happened there and why?
Oh, yeah, he told me I had to play the cornet or (unintelligible) else get out of here. Wasn't nothing else to it.
And the other point about your age compared with the other people in the band. You were about what age and they were older?
I see, oh, how old was I. They were adults.
Around 35 or 40.
Yes, around 35 or 40.
And you were how old?
I was about 10 or 11 or 12.
Well, I can see the point when you said your father wanted you to be there and do more or less what he wanted.
I had to do it.
But I was thinking you were 17 or so, but I can see, he said, you will be there.
Get swatted in the face, he'd jump on you too.
Well Look at all the training you got though.
He was a good trainer. Very good.
(Inaudible) band you and your brother had.
At night, with your brother Dean.
Yeah.
You were playing what, more jazz,
more dance music.?
Dance music. So in the park concerts --

So you were developing in both sides as you were coming up, because as you see, most musicians are in one or the other. It's hard to switch back and forth if you play classical music all your life and try to play jazz like when you play jazz and try to go to classical, but and you were coming up with both sides at the same time.
You had to learn, you do like your parents tell you to do, if you didn't do that --
Your father a musician, your uncle, you had it all around you.
Sure, they'd knock you out.
